quiz.q: In the troposphere temperature falls about…
The speed of sound at sea level is about…
Density at 11 km is about what fraction of sea level?
Mach number is…
quiz.why: Speed divided by the local speed of sound.

quiz.q: The speed of sound depends on pressure.
quiz.why: For an ideal gas it depends only on temperature.

quiz.q: It gets colder all the way up.
quiz.why: Temperature levels off above 11 km and rises again higher in the stratosphere.

quiz.q: Thinner air always helps.
quiz.why: It cuts drag but also lift and engine thrust, so wings must fly faster or at higher lift coefficients.

quiz.q: An airliner flies at 230 m/s true airspeed at 11 km. What is its Mach number?
Find the air density at 11,000 m with the NASA model (T = −56.46 °C, p = 22.72 kPa). Give your answer in kg/m³.
Find the temperature at 1,500 m in the NASA model. Give your answer in °C.
What is Mach 2 at sea level in m/s?
Find the sea-level density from p = 101.40 kPa and T = 15.04 °C. Give your answer in kg/m³.
T ≈ −17.4 °C, p ≈ 54.1 kPa, ρ ≈ 0.738 kg/m³ (60% of sea level).
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit. Find T, p and ρ at 5,000 m with NASA’s model.

quiz.q: 340 m/s and 295 m/s.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit. Find the speed of sound at sea level (15 °C) and at 11 km (−56.5 °C).

quiz.q: Aircraft fly where weather and climate happen. NASA studies aircraft emissions through computer modeling, combustion laboratory testing and flight testing, because what engines release at altitude matters for the atmosphere.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: The same atmosphere physics underlies how satellites turn the radiation they measure into profiles of the air’s temperature.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: A standard atmosphere is an average model fitted to measurements. In NASA’s model the troposphere runs from the ground to 11,000 m, and temperature falls about 6.5 °C per kilometer.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: From 11 to 25 km (lower stratosphere) the model’s temperature is constant at −56.46 °C, while pressure keeps falling exponentially.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: Density follows from the ideal-gas law, ρ = p/(RT). At 11 km air is about 30% as dense as at sea level.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: The speed of sound is a = √(γRT), so it depends only on temperature. Mach number M = V/a.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.
